extracted.intended_audience: the people/voters and policymakers considering ratification of the U.S. Constitution (readers of the New York Packet)
extracted.subtask_description: A normative critique of the proposed federal Constitution focusing on the proper allocation and scope of national powers (especially for common defense), the needed organization of government, and the practicability of constitutional restraints. Written as persuasive guidance for citizens deciding on ratification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Energetic government necessary to preserve the Union
rubrics_metrics.description: THE necessity of a Constitution, at least equally energetic with the one proposed, to the preservation of the Union, is the point at the examination of which we are now arrived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The federal government must be sufficiently energetic to secure the Union; if the Union is to be durable and wide in extent, a vigorous national government is required rather than a loose confederacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify objects proper for federal government
rubrics_metrics.description: The principal purposes to be answered by union are these--the common defense of the members; the preservation of the public peace as well against internal convulsions as external attacks; the regulation of commerce with other nations and between the States; the superintendence of our intercourse, political and commercial, with foreign countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These enumerated objects (defense, public peace, interstate and international commerce, foreign intercourse) define the legitimate sphere of federal authority and should guide allocation of powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Powers essential to common defense must be plenary and adaptable
rubrics_metrics.description: The authorities essential to the common defense are these: to raise armies; to build and equip fleets; to prescribe rules for the government of both; to direct their operations; to provide for their support. These powers ought to exist without limitation, BECAUSE IT IS IMPOSSIBLE TO FORESEE OR DEFINE THE EXTENT AND VARIETY OF NATIONAL EXIGENCIES.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because national exigencies are unforeseeable, constitutional shackles on defense powers are unwise; the means must be coextensive with the possible combinations of circumstances and under the direction of the councils charged with defense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Means ought to be proportioned to the end
rubrics_metrics.description: The MEANS ought to be proportioned to the END; the persons, from whose agency the attainment of any END is expected, ought to possess the MEANS by which it is to be attained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assigning authority, ensure that the agents charged with an objective have adequate powers and resources to accomplish it; otherwise the objective (e.g., national defense) cannot be reliably achieved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal laws must bind individuals as well as States
rubrics_metrics.description: We must extend the laws of the federal government to the individual citizens of America; we must discard the fallacious scheme of quotas and requisitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relying on state legislatures to implement federal requisitions is impracticable; to secure compliance and efficacy, federal laws should act directly on individuals rather than only on states as collective entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ratification should rest on the consent of the people, not solely state legislatures
rubrics_metrics.description: The fabric of American empire ought to rest on the solid basis of THE CONSENT OF THE PEOPLE. The streams of national power ought to flow immediately from that pure, original fountain of all legitimate authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A national government founded only on state-legislature ratification risks instability (e.g., doctrines of repeal); popular ratification provides firmer legitimacy and reduces disputes about validity of federal powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislature (not Executive alone) should have authority over raising armies with appropriation safeguards
rubrics_metrics.description: It will be surprised to discover... that the whole power of raising armies was lodged in the LEGISLATURE, not in the EXECUTIVE; that this legislature was to be a popular body... and that... forbids the appropriation of money for the support of an army for any longer period than two years -- a precaution... against the keeping up of troops without evident necessity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confer military-raising power to the representative legislature while retaining appropriations controls (e.g., limitation of funding to short terms) as a check against permanent forces kept without oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid impracticable constitutional restraints on military establishments
rubrics_metrics.description: From a close examination it will appear that restraints upon the discretion of the legislature in respect to military establishments in time of peace, would be improper to be imposed, and if imposed, from the necessities of society, would be unlikely to be observed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not enshrine absolute prohibitions in the constitution that public necessity will routinely require breaching; such clauses either become dead letters or encourage subversion of constitutional reverence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vague prohibitions (e.g., 'no standing armies') are ineffective and ambiguous
rubrics_metrics.description: If it be confined to the latter it will have no precise signification, and it will be ineffectual for the purpose intended. When armies are once raised what shall be denominated 'keeping them up'... Who shall judge of the continuance of the danger?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid constitutional language that creates irresolvable questions of interpretation (e.g., what counts as 'keeping up' an army), since it invites evasion and judicial/political conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: National possession of military forces prevents interstate rivalry and usurpation
rubrics_metrics.description: If the State governments should possess separate and independent military forces... military establishments, nourished by mutual jealousy, would be apt to swell beyond their natural or proper size... they would be engines for the abridgment or demolition of the national authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Centralize the principal military establishments in the national government to prevent powerful states from using armed forces to challenge or subvert the Union; separate state armies risk imbalance and conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Militia alone cannot be relied on for national defense; professional forces are required
rubrics_metrics.description: The militia... had like to have lost us our independence... The steady operations of war against a regular and disciplined army can only be successfully conducted by a force of the same kind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relying solely on part-time militias is imprudent; sustained, disciplined, professional armed forces (army/navy) are necessary for effective defense and for economy, stability, and vigor in prolonged operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocate powers so each level has sufficient authority for its assigned objects
rubrics_metrics.description: If the circumstances of our country are such as to demand a compound instead of a simple... government, the essential point... will be to discriminate the OBJECTS... which shall appertain to the different provinces or departments of power; allowing to each the most ample authority for fulfilling the objects committed to its charge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When dividing authority between national and state governments, allocate each office/policy area a degree of power commensurate with its responsibilities; failure to do so produces inefficiency and insecurity.
